problem: Given that the polynomial $f(x)=18{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}-16x-3$ has a root in the interval $(1,3),$ find the sum of the **distinct** real roots of $f(x).$
worked_solution:
Given a polynomial with integer coefficients, the rational roots theorem states that any rational roots of the polynomial must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of the constant term}}{\text{factor of the leading coefficient}}.
$$

For the given polynomial $f(x),$ the constant term is $-3$ and the leading coefficient is $18.$ So, any rational roots of $f(x)$ must take the form

$$
\pm \frac{\text{factor of }-3}{\text{factor of }18}.
$$

Therefore, the possible rational roots are as follows:

$$
\pm \frac{1}{18},\,\pm \frac{1}{9},\,\pm \frac{1}{6},\,\pm \frac{1}{3},\,\pm \frac{1}{2},\,\pm 1,\,\pm \frac{3}{2},\,\pm 3.
$$

Of these roots, the only root in the interval $(1,3)$ is $\frac{3}{2}.$

Using the synthetic division, we get the following:

|  | ${x}^{3}$ | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\frac{3}{2}$ | $18$ | $-15$ | $-16$ | $-3$ |
|  | $↓$ | $27$ | $18$ | $3$ |
|  | $18$ | $12$ | $2$ | $0$ |

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(x-\frac{3}{2})(18{x}^{2}+12x+2).\end{aligned}
$$

Since the highest-degree factor is now a quadratic, we can continue factoring using the usual methods:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(x-\frac{3}{2})(18{x}^{2}+12x+2) \\  & =2(x-\frac{3}{2})(9{x}^{2}+6x+1) \\  & =(2x-3)(3x+1)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the factors equal to $0,$ we find the roots $x=-\frac{1}{3},\frac{3}{2}.$ Summing these roots, we get

$$
-\frac{1}{3}+\frac{3}{2}=\frac{7}{6}.
$$
